meta.title: Redfacil · The settlement network for your payment
meta.description: Prototype that recommends which blockchain network to settle a payment on in Colombia, using the thesis model and explainable risk traffic lights.

footer.demo: Academic prototype. Recommendations use the thesis model with baseline measurements (Polygon, Celo and Arbitrum: 90 days, October 2026; Tempo, Aptos and Canton: preliminary benchmark) and override them with live metrics when they are current. Peso costs use a demo exchange rate and exclude on and off ramps.
footer.academic: Degree project. Visually inspired by the Bancolombia palette, with no affiliation to the institution.

E1.name: Remittances
E1.desc: Transfers of USD 200 to 500 abroad. Cost rules; waiting hours is acceptable.

E2.name: Domestic commerce
E2.desc: Purchases of COP 15,000 to 159,456. Latency rules: seconds, as with Bre-B.

E3.name: High value
E3.desc: Settlements above COP 100 million. Concentration and irreversibility rule.

polygon.desc: Proof-of-stake layer 1. Wenia issues COPW on it. Four addresses produce its blocks.

celo.desc: Layer 2 on the OP stack since March 2025, with a single sequencer and fees that can be paid in stablecoins.

arbitrum.desc: Optimistic layer 2 rollup with a single sequencer; state is only irreversible after a dispute window of about 6 days.

tempo.desc: EVM-compatible, permissioned layer 1 built for payments, without a volatile native token. Measured in a preliminary pass.

aptos.desc: General-purpose layer 1 with the Move virtual machine and deterministic finality. Measured in a preliminary pass.

canton.desc: Platform with no global chain for institutional finance. With a stablecoin, a third party cannot verify the payment.

provenance.title: Where the data come from
provenance.thesis: Each metric says whether its value is live (a recent query to the network) or from the baseline measurement: Polygon, Celo and Arbitrum, the thesis 90-day window; Tempo, Aptos and Canton, the preliminary reduced-sample benchmark.
provenance.benchmark: What cannot be computed live (for example finality on Ethereum or 72-hour windows that are still filling) keeps the baseline measurement and is tagged as such. See the Monitor for details.

result.disclaimer: This recommendation is a preliminary result of an academic prototype. It is not financial advice, it does not reflect real-time network data and costs exclude the on and off ramps to pesos.

sem1.title: Network traffic light
sem1.sub: Summary for your payment: it depends on the aggregate score and the gates.

sem2.title: Your payment by rating block
sem2.sub: Open each block to see its measured metrics, the target and the unacceptable limit.
sem2.rule: A metric is green when it meets the target (score 1), red at or beyond the unacceptable limit (score 0) and yellow in between. A block is green with a score of 0.70 or more and red below 0.45. The network is red if it fails a gate; otherwise its color comes from the median of its score over 10,000 replicas. Scores are those of the thesis model.

standard.title: Rating standard
standard.sub: How each network is rated: the thesis model with a traffic light on top. It is public, fixed and reproducible: the same payment always gives the same result.
standard.demoNote: Thresholds and weights are those of the thesis model and are read from the backend. The uncertainty of each metric is the measured one when it exists (standard error of the live sample or of the thesis); Tempo, Aptos and Canton baseline measurements have no estimate and are treated as exact.

green.name: Green
green.desc: One of the best options: a score of 0.70 or more.

yellow.name: Yellow
yellow.desc: A good option, with points to watch.

red.name: Red
red.desc: Do not send through this network: it fails a gate, the recipient does not accept it or its score is below 0.45.

model.title: The model in six steps
model.s1: Each metric becomes a score from 0 to 1 on a logarithmic scale between its target (t) and its unacceptable limit (w).
model.s2: Gates G1 to G4 discard inadmissible networks: they get no score, not a zero.
model.s3: Metrics are averaged within each block; blocks are combined with a weighted geometric mean with a 0.05 floor.
model.s4: The payment is described with four attributes and its weights are interpolated between the three scenarios by similarity.
model.s5: Certainty κ says how well the scenarios represent the payment: high from 0.75, medium from 0.45.
model.s6: 10,000 replicas perturb measurements and weights; two networks are in different bands only if one beats the other with probability 0.85 or more.

scenarios.title: Reference scenarios
scenarios.note: The thesis defines three scenarios. Payments under COP 15,000 are treated as commerce (E2): the amount is clipped to COP 10,000 for weighting, but the cost is computed on the real amount.

standard.ext: Own extension; not part of the score

limits.title: What it does not cover
limits.body: It does not measure each network's institutional continuity, regulatory compliance, the cost of entering and leaving pesos or the real maximum capacity. With a single node provider per network, a provider error would go unnoticed.

notes.noCongestion: There was no congestion in the window, so the slope cannot be estimated.
notes.unreliableRegression: The regression on the reduced sample is not reliable; excluded.
notes.anchorSplit: The gas of the Ethereum publications is split among the transfers they cover.
notes.noDisputeWindow: No dispute window: irreversibility coincides with publication.
notes.disputeWindow: Irreversible after the dispute window plus confirmation time.
notes.lowerBound: Lower bound: it measures observed demand, not maximum capacity.
notes.documentary: Conservative bound from official incidents (the only documentary metric).
notes.singleSequencer: A single sequencer produces the blocks.
notes.signedAuth: Almost all of it comes from signed authorizations sent by a third party who pays the fee.
notes.paymasters: Most of it comes from ERC-4337 paymasters.
notes.strictMemo: Strict version: only memos added to direct transfers of the asset.
notes.roundedSeconds: Timestamps are whole seconds: with 0.25 s blocks there is rounding error.
notes.reducedSample: Reduced sample of minutes, not the full window; no bootstrap.
notes.noAnchor: It does not anchor its state on Ethereum: there is no anchoring cost.
notes.liveShortRun: Live polling of 30 seconds, not the 72 hours of the plan.
notes.configuredCapacity: Configured capacity derived from network state, an optimistic upper bound; rescaled to 18 TPS.
notes.permissioned: Permissioned network: the proposer is chosen by VRF even though the set is small.
notes.notComparable: Measured differently from the thesis; not comparable and excluded.
notes.degenerate: Determined by the architecture (no native token), not by user behavior.
notes.contaminated: Probably contaminated by fee splitting or collateral rebalancing.
notes.frozenOracle: APT price frozen in the oracle since 26 August 2026.
notes.finalityNotMeasured: Finality could not be measured by HTTP polling: a block lasts ~20 ms.
notes.memoNotDefined: What counts as a valid reference on Aptos is still to be fixed.
notes.burstWindow: The window fell in a periodic burst of reports, not payment traffic.
notes.memberAllocation: Free allocation per member; it underestimates the real capacity of the synchronizer.
notes.svWeights: Computed on super validator weights, not on blocks.
notes.stablecoinNotObservable: With a stablecoin under the token standard, a third party cannot verify the payment (partial estimate).

data.centralScore: Model score with every metric at its measured value (no simulation): {score}. The band score is the median of 10,000 replicas.

gates.title: Admissibility gates
gates.sub: A network that fails an applicable gate is inadmissible: it gets no score.
gates.notApplicable: Does not apply to this payment

G1.desc: No greater than 20 s (the payment is mostly commerce).

G2.name: Verifiable finality
G2.desc: A third party can verify inclusion and irreversibility.

G3.name: Reconciliation reference
G3.desc: A memo is in use (D2 greater than zero).

G4.name: Capacity
G4.desc: The capacity margin is not below 1 (only if B3 measures capacity).

gates.allPass: No gate fails for this payment.

liveData.title: Network monitor
liveData.sub: Live metrics per network, where each value comes from and what is missing. Metrics that cannot be measured live stay on the baseline until you recalibrate.
liveData.error: The backend could not be reached.
liveData.staleBackend: No connection to the backend: showing the last known data.
liveData.legend: Live: value computed from recent queries to the network. Base: stored long measurement (thesis or benchmark). No data: neither live nor in the baseline.
liveData.noCollector: This collector has not reported yet.
liveData.samples: Stored samples: {blocks} blocks, {txs} transactions, {finality} finality readings

why.valida: the live value is not current
why.insuficiente: not enough samples yet; using the baseline
why.obsoleta: the live value expired; using the baseline
why.fallida: the live read failed; using the baseline
why.solo_base: only exists in the baseline measurement

tag.liveTitle: Computed live {age} ago from {n} samples over a {window} window
tag.baseWhy: Baseline measurement: the live value is {state}

banner.baseMode: Measurement mode: baseline measurements only, no live data.
banner.baseOnly: No current live metrics: this recommendation uses baseline measurements only.
banner.stale: Could not refresh: showing the last known result.

insufficient.title: Not enough data to recommend
insufficient.body: The model needs at least two networks with measurements. No recommendation is shown so none is made up.

recalibrate.title: Recalibrate baseline measurements
recalibrate.desc: Re-runs the batch benchmark (collection, computation and deliverables) and rebuilds the baseline measurements of Tempo, Aptos and Canton; for Polygon, Celo and Arbitrum it backfills the recent window (blocks, payments and Ethereum anchoring) so their live metrics fill faster. Everything that can be measured in near real time already updates by itself; this only renews the fallback. Aptos without an API key takes several minutes because of the service rate limit.

simulation.title: Simulated-user tests
simulation.sub: Twelve user profiles evaluated with the unmodified thesis model: who the recommended network serves and how stable that answer is. This page refreshes itself.
simulation.staleBackend: No connection to the backend: showing the last known data.
simulation.empty: No results yet: no test batch has completed. Once one runs, it will appear here.

run.title: Batch shown
run.line: Batch {id} · {evals} evaluations · seed {seed} · {reps} replicas · panel of {panel} per profile · finished {age} ago

fit.title: Coverage and fit to the need (P1, P2)
fit.sub: For each profile: which network the model recommends and whether it meets what the user needs. Preference accepts inclusion in a block; requirement demands finality.
fit.legend: Meets: all of band 1 satisfies the need. Partial: tie and only some networks meet it. Gap: no band-1 network meets it but another admissible one does. No solution: no admissible network meets it. Not evaluable: data missing.

counter.title: Does the winner depend on how it was measured? (P3) and a network going down (P4)
counter.sub: Share of panel users whose recommended network changes against the reference.
counter.aptosHint: Share of users where Aptos would beat the best other network if its finality could be measured.

sens.title: User sensitivity (P5)
sens.sub: Share of users whose recommended network changes when a single payment attribute changes.

conv.title: Replica convergence (P6)
conv.sub: Agreement with the run that uses the most replicas. Shows how many replicas are needed.

panel.title: Continuous panel (P7)
panel.sub: The same users are re-evaluated every cycle on the live network: any change can only come from the network.
panel.stabilityHint: Share of evaluations whose band 1 did not change between consecutive cycles.
panel.differsHint: Share of users with a different band 1 than on the baseline.
panel.invalidHint: Cycles with fewer than half the expected live metrics; they do not count in the indicators.
panel.empty: The continuous panel has not produced cycles yet.
panel.strip: Each bar is a cycle: green no changes, yellow with changes, grey invalid.

simulation.disclaimer: Profiles are design assumptions (only the centers of profiles 1 to 3 come from the thesis); results are read per profile, never as a share of the population. A poor fit is evidence to discuss, not a demonstrated flaw in the model.
